findings.issue_text: **`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:35-40, 158-165`** — Calendar update uses the *requesting* user's identity/credentials, not the booking organizer's, even though the handler explicitly fetches `booking.user.credentials` via `include` and never uses it. `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({ ...user, ... })` both use `ctx.user` (the caller). The auth check right above this (`isTeamAdminOrOwner`, `isAttendee`) explicitly supports team admins/owners and attendees calling this endpoint — but for any of those callers, the calendar sync will run under the wrong account's (or an unrelated) calendar credentials rather than the organizer's, so the actual calendar invite likely won't be updated correctly. This call is also *not* wrapped in the try/catch that guards email sending, so a failure here throws a raw 500 back to the client **after** the `prisma.booking.update` has already committed the new attendee rows — leaving the DB and calendar out of sync with no rollback, while the user sees a hard error for what is (from the DB's perspective) a successful add.

Fix: build `EventManager` from `booking.user` (the organizer) and its already-fetched `credentials`, not `ctx.user`; wrap `updateCalendarAttendees` in error handling (or a transaction/compensating action) so a calendar-sync failure doesn't leave the DB attendee list silently ahead of the calendar state.

**`addGuests.handler.ts:46-48`** — `isTeamAdminOrOwner = isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. The variable name and evident intent ("is admin OR owner") call for `||`, but the code uses `&&`. If `isTeamAdmin` includes owners (typical in this codebase's role model), this silently restricts the permission to team *owners only*, locking out legitimate team admins — contradicting both the name and the apparent design goal.
Fix: change to `||`, or clarify with two separately-named booleans if AND was genuinely intended.

**`addGuests.handler.ts:70-78`** — Email comparisons are case-sensitive. `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lower-cased, but `guest` (raw user input) is not, so `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` fails to catch case-variant blacklisted addresses (e.g. blacklist has `spam@x.com`, submission of `SPAM@x.com` slips through). Likewise `guest === attendee.email` for de-dup against existing attendees is case-sensitive, so `John@x.com` can be added as a "new" guest even though `john@x.com` is already an attendee, producing a duplicate/near-duplicate attendee record.
Fix: normalize both sides (`.toLowerCase()`) before comparing.

**`email-manager.ts:525-550` vs `email-manager.ts:495-524`** — `sendAddGuestsEmails` is a near copy of `sendLocationChangeEmails` but drops the `eventTypeDisableHostEmail`/`eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` checks that its sibling (and `sendRequestRescheduleEmail` above it) respects. Organizers/attendees who disabled notifications for this event type will still be emailed on every guest addition, a regression relative to the pattern this code was clearly modeled on.
Fix: thread `eventTypeMetadata` through from the handler and gate the sends the same way the neighboring functions do.

**`addGuests.handler.ts:74-90` / `addGuests.schema.ts:1-8`** — The backend never rejects duplicates *within* a single submitted `guests` array — it only filters against pre-existing attendees. The uniqueness check lives solely in the frontend (`AddGuestsDialog.tsx`'s local `ZAddGuestsInputSchema.refine`). Since this is a public authed tRPC mutation reachable directly (not just through the dialog), a request with `guests: ["a@x.com", "a@x.com"]` (both new) would pass the schema and handler filtering and attempt to `createMany` two identical attendee rows.
Fix: dedupe/validate uniqueness server-side too (e.g. move the `.refine` into the shared `addGuests.schema.ts` used by both client and server).

No tests were added anywhere in this diff — not for `addGuestsHandler` (permission branches, blacklist/dedup logic, email dispatch), not for `AddGuestsDialog`/`MultiEmail`, not for the new email templates. This is a booking-mutating, multi-actor-authorized endpoint with several edge cases (exactly the kind of logic that regresses silently without coverage).
Fix: add handler unit tests covering the three permission branches, blacklist/dedup/case-sensitivity behavior, and a component test for `AddGuestsDialog`'s validation states.

**`AddGuestsDialog.tsx:36-39`** — `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")`: `message` is built from a template literal (`` `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` ``) so it's always truthy; the `t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback is dead code.

**`addGuests.handler.ts:55`** — `TRPCError({ code: "FORBIDDEN", message: "you_do_not_have_permission" })` is passed through `t(err.message)` on the frontend, but `"you_do_not_have_permission"` is not a key in `apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json`; the user will see the raw key text instead of a translated message.

**`addGuests.handler.ts:167-171`** — Email-send failures are swallowed with a bare `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` — no error object, no logger integration, making production diagnosis harder.

**`addGuests.handler.ts:80-81`** — When `uniqueGuests` is empty because all submitted addresses were already attendees or blacklisted (not because they were duplicates/invalid emails), the thrown message is still `emails_must_be_unique_valid`, which mischaracterizes the actual reason to the user.

**`AddGuestsDialog.tsx:14`** vs **`addGuests.schema.ts:1-8`** — Validation logic is duplicated and has drifted (frontend adds a uniqueness `.refine`, backend schema doesn't); the frontend schema is also rebuilt on every render instead of being hoisted out of the component.
**`addGuests.handler.ts:83-90`** — New guests are inserted with `name: ""` since `MultiEmail` only collects email addresses; minor display gap in attendee lists.
**`BookingListItem.tsx:194-201, 553-554`** — "Add guests" is exposed even for `isBookingInPast && isConfirmed` (already-completed meetings), which may not be a meaningful use case worth surfacing.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, `uniqueGuests` is computed by filtering out emails that are already in `booking.attendees` and any that are in `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`. If all submitted emails are filtered out for either of those reasons (or even if `guests` is an empty array), `uniqueGuests.length === 0` triggers a `TRPCError` with message key `emails_must_be_unique_valid`. That message implies invalid/duplicate emails, but the code path can be reached when emails are valid yet already attendees or explicitly blacklisted, so the error text can mislead the user.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`AddGuestsDialog.tsx:14`** vs **`addGuests.schema.ts:1-8`** — Validation logic is duplicated and has drifted (frontend adds a uniqueness `.refine`, backend schema doesn't); the frontend schema is also rebuilt on every render instead of being hoisted out of the component.

adjudication.rationale:
The diff shows two separate Zod schemas for the same “add guests” input with different rules: `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` builds `z.array(z.string().email()).refine(...)` to enforce uniqueness, while the server input schema `addGuests.schema.ts` only uses `z.array(z.string().email())` and does not enforce uniqueness. This is verifiable drift/duplication.

This mismatch matters because the server handler does not actually de-duplicate the `guests` array: `uniqueGuests = guests.filter(...)` only filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails, but preserves duplicates within the request (e.g. `["a@x.com","a@x.com"]` remains duplicated). That can lead to duplicate attendee creates or a DB error depending on constraints, so relying on frontend-only uniqueness validation is a real correctness issue.

Also, the frontend schema is defined inside the component, so it is recreated on every render; that’s a minor but real inefficiency visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`BookingListItem.tsx:194-201, 553-554`** — "Add guests" is exposed even for `isBookingInPast && isConfirmed` (already-completed meetings), which may not be a meaningful use case worth surfacing.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an "add_members" action to the `actions` array unconditionally, but the proposed finding claims it is incorrectly exposed specifically for `isBookingInPast && isConfirmed`. In the provided diff, there is no logic shown that gates actions based on `isBookingInPast`/`isConfirmed`, nor any requirement evidenced that adding guests to past confirmed bookings is invalid. The finding is essentially a product/UX opinion ("may not be meaningful") rather than a verifiable defect introduced by the change.
